jobs.title: Deployed Engineer (Early Career- SF)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

This team works directly with companies building and running AI agents in production, helping turn ideas and prototypes into systems teams can rely on.

This is a hands-on, highly technical team that partners closely with customer engineers across the full lifecycle, from pre-sales evaluations to post-deployment advisory work. The focus is on achieving the technical win, co-designing agent architectures, and helping customers operate agents reliably at scale using the LangChain suite.

Deployed Engineers sit at the intersection of engineering, product, and go-to-market, shaping how LangChain is adopted in the field and feeding real-world insights back into the platform.

You'll work on some of the hardest problems in applied AI alongside customers. You will help customers adopt innovative new practices in agentic engineering, and ensure they ship reliable agents into production, quickly. The feedback loop is fast, the impact is visible, and your work directly shapes how AI agents are built in the real world.

What You’ll Do

  • Co-architect and co-build production AI agents with customer engineering teams and customers

  • Own the technical win in pre-sales by designing POCs, answering deep technical questions, and guiding evaluations

  • Help customers deploy and operate agent-based applications such as conversational agents, research agents, and multi-step workflows

  • Advise customers post-sale on architecture, best practices, and roadmap-level decisions

  • Build and run tailored demos, trainings, and workshops for developer audiences

  • Surface field feedback and contribute reusable patterns, cookbooks, and example code that scale across customers

  • Interface with LangChain's engineering, product and design (EPD) team to share field perspectives and guide product direction based on customer priorities

  • Occasionally contribute code upstream when it meaningfully improves customer outcomes

  • This role requires 40% travel to customer sites to support deployment, onboarding, and ongoing technical engagement

What You’ll Bring

  • 1-3 years of experience in software engineering, customer engineering, solutions engineering, founding engineering, or a similarly technical role, ideally at a startup or high-growth company

  • Strong Python, JavaScript and systems fundamentals

  • Hands-on experience building and deploying agent-based or LLM-powered applications beyond simple API calls, including multi-step workflows, orchestration, and failure handling

  • Strong technical communication skills and builder credibility; Can explain technical tradeoffs clearly, translate complex AI concepts into actionable insights, and build trust with technical customers and engineering teams

  • Excited to work directly with customers during POCs, architecture reviews, and technical evaluations

  • Take responsibility for outcomes, not just recommendations

  • Have a bias toward action and enjoy figuring things out as you go

  • Are excited about shipping AI agents in production

Nice to Have’s:

  • You’ve deployed AI agents in production, especially using LangChain, LangGraph, or similar frameworks

  • Worked with LLM evaluation, observability, or guardrails

  • Have experience with cloud environments (AWS, GCP, Azure), containers, and Kubernetes concepts

  • Have shipped and operated production software and are comfortable owning systems under real-world constraints

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

About the Role

We’re hiring Sales Development Representatives to join our founding SDR team and help shape the future of how companies adopt LangChain. As part of our SDR team, you’ll turn high inbound interest and targeted outbound demand into qualified opportunities and create an exceptional first-touch experiences for prospects.

You’ll work closely with our Marketing, Sales, and Operations alongside using LangChain and LangGraph-powered agents to automate list building, enrichment, and outreach freeing you to focus entirely on high-impact prospecting and conversations with teams exploring agentic AI.

What makes this role different: You’ll drive pipeline and revenue while learning to leverage AI, automation, and LangChain itself to become a next-generation GTM operator.

  • Follow up with inbound and outbound prospects via phone, email, and LinkedIn to uncover fit, needs, and potential value.

  • Partner closely with Account Executives to hand off qualified opportunities and ensure a smooth buyer experience.

  • Experiment with new channels, messaging, and automation to continuously increase conversion and efficiency.

  • Use LangChain powered agents to test, learn, and improve prospecting strategies

What You’ll Bring

  • 1–2 years of experience in a Sales, SDR, or BDR role within SaaS or technology (or strong curiosity and drive if you’re early in your career)

  • Motivated by learning, iteration, and experimentation you treat outreach like a craft

  • Excited about modern sales tech, AI tools, and shaping how next-generation GTM teams operate

  • Positive, persistent, and highly organized you follow up, follow through, and bring energy to every interaction

jobs.title: Product Manager, Monetization
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

The Monetization team sits at the center of LangChain's growth engine. We own the systems, surfaces, and strategies that connect the value of LangSmith to revenue — from pricing and packaging to billing infrastructure, upgrade flows, and the product mechanics that move users from free to paid to enterprise. We work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Finance to make sure the way we charge for our platform reflects the value it delivers and scales as our customers scale.

 

We're looking for a Product Manager to own monetization across LangSmith. This is a high-leverage, high-visibility role: you'll define how we price and package a rapidly evolving platform, build the in-product experiences that drive conversion and expansion, and make sure our billing infrastructure keeps pace with the business.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own the end-to-end monetization product surface: pricing pages, upgrade flows, usage dashboards, billing management, and the in-app signals that drive conversion and expansion.

  • Define and iterate on LangSmith's pricing and packaging — usage-based, seat-based, or hybrid — in close partnership with Finance, Sales, and leadership.

  • Instrument and analyze the funnel: identify where users drop off, where expansion signals appear, and what product changes move the needle on activation, retention, and revenue.

  • Build the billing and entitlement infrastructure alongside engineering — usage metering, plan enforcement, trial mechanics, and enterprise contract support.

  • Partner with the Sales and Solutions Engineering teams to understand enterprise buying motions and design packaging that maps cleanly to how large organizations buy software.

  • Translate customer conversations and data signals into crisp requirements; ship iteratively and measure impact.

  • Help shape LangChain's broader go-to-market strategy alongside our founders and leadership team.

 

What You'll Bring

  • 4+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time spent on monetization, growth, or platform pricing at a B2B SaaS or developer-tools company.

  • Strong analytical instincts — you're comfortable in the data, know which metrics matter, and can tell the difference between a signal and noise.

  • Experience working on billing, entitlements, or usage-based pricing systems, and an appreciation for the technical complexity underneath them.

  • A sharp intuition for the developer and enterprise buyer experience — you understand that a pricing page and a checkout flow are product problems, not just marketing ones.

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and move quickly: you can go from a rough hypothesis to a shipped experiment without needing everything to be perfectly defined first.

  • Genuine curiosity about the AI/LLM space and how the infrastructure layer is evolving — you don't need to have worked in AI, but you need to want to learn it fast.

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

jobs.title: Partner Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

Cloud providers and Systems Integrators help LangChain reach customers that our direct sales and customer engineering teams can't reach on their own. This role is the technical foundation behind that ecosystem.

You'll build the reference architectures, integration patterns, and enablement programs that make partner motions work technically: co-sell with cloud hyperscalers, and independent delivery capability at systems integrators and global systems integrators (GSIs). You build with and for a partner, whose technical team then takes what you built to dozens of their own clients.


What You'll Do

Cloud partner engineering (AWS, GCP, Azure)

  • Own the technical relationship with partner and field teams at AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure

  • Build reference architectures and integration patterns for running LangChain, LangGraph, DeepAgents and LangSmith on each cloud, including integrations with each provider's native AI and data services (for example Amazon Bedrock, Gemini Enterprise, AzureAI)

  • Support the technical side of co-sell: joint solution briefs, deployment guides, and validated architectures that cloud sellers can bring to their customers

  • Partner with cloud account teams on solutioning for named accounts, from discovery through technical win

  • Keep our marketplace listings, deployment options, and co-sell technical assets current as the product evolves

  • Enable cloud field and partner teams through workshops, demos, and technical briefings so they can position LangChain without pulling in our engineers for every deal

  • Build and maintain joint technical plans with each cloud provider, turning shared account and industry priorities into a concrete set of reference assets

Marketplace motions with services partners

  • Support systems integrators and resellers when they're part of a cloud deal, such as marketplace private offers transacted through a channel partner or joint deployments on a customer's cloud

  • Give those partners the technical assets they need to scope and deliver LangChain on AWS, GCP, or Azure, using existing reference architectures and implementation guides rather than a standalone enablement program

Partner technical evangelism and feedback

  • Serve as a technical escalation point for complex deployments sourced through cloud partners

  • Represent LangChain at cloud provider events, summits, and joint webinars

  • Gather feedback from cloud partners and the field, and route it back to product and engineering

What You'll Bring

7+ years of experience in a technical, partner-facing or customer-facing role such as Partner Engineer, Partner Solutions Architect, Solutions Architect, or Sales Engineer. Experience at or alongside a hyperscaler is a strong plus. We also like former founders and technical leaders, so if you have an unusual background but the right skill set, you're welcome to apply.

Cloud and partner experience

  • Track record of working with AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure partner and field teams to drive co-sell, from joint solution design through technical win

  • Familiarity with cloud marketplace mechanics such as listings, private offers, and channel partner offers, and with hyperscaler co-sell programs

  • Experience enabling a partner's field or technical teams so they can position and deploy a product without depending on you for every deal

  • Comfortable working across engineering, partnerships, and sales at the same time

  • Strong presentation and technical communication skills, able to translate between technical and business stakeholders, including C-suite executives

Agent engineering and development

  • Hands-on experience building with LLM frameworks such as langchain, langgraph, or similar, including RAG patterns and agent architecture

  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks and iterating on prompts and agent behavior based on results

jobs.title: Business Systems Analyst, GTM Systems
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

You'll join our GTM Systems team, which owns the systems LangChain's go-to-market actually runs on — Salesforce above all: the account and contact model, territory and routing, the sales process from first touch to closed-won, and the quote-to-cash and provisioning stack behind it.

We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next.

You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale.

This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates.

You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan.

You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct.

Location: San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph.

What You'll Do

Carry multi-quarter programs

  • Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption.

  • Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs.

  • Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets.

Own what gets specified and what ships

  • Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation.

  • Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off.

  • Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build.

Protect revenue data integrity

  • Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them.

  • Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions.

  • Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production.

What Success Looks Like:

In your first 6–12 months, you might:

  • Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field.

  • Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale.

  • Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation.

  • Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against.

  • Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution.

What You'll Bring

Systems and domain depth

  • Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout.

  • Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene.

  • Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes.

  • Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code.

Program leadership

  • Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day.

  • Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release.

  • Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality.

  • Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative.

Judgment and communication

  • One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec.

  • Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket.

  • AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way.

  • Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it.

Nice to Have's

None of these is a screen; any one makes you useful faster.

  • You've owned a core Salesforce object domain — Account, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity — through a full redesign.

  • You've traced a Salesforce field into a usage record into a provisioning step, and seen what broke downstream when it moved.

  • You've worked with cloud marketplace operations — AWS or GCP private offers, co-sell, entitlement mapping, metering, and the failure modes when they break.

  • You've worked with usage-based billing systems such as Metronome, Orb, or similar, and CRM↔billing identity reconciliation.

  • You have LangChain or LangGraph experience, or you're excited to learn it here from the people who build it.

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Solutions Marketing Lead to shape how LangChain brings its full platform to priority industries, enterprise buyers, and high-value use cases.

This role sits at the intersection of product and GTM. You’ll translate customer problems into clear solution narratives, repeatable sales plays, campaign themes, and customer-facing assets that help teams understand where LangChain fits in their AI strategy.

You’ll develop industry solutions, use case solutions, and enterprise solution stories for segments such as financial services, healthcare, life sciences, and other priority markets. You’ll work closely with sales, solutions, product, demand generation, field marketing, education, and customer teams to understand what matters in the field, turn those insights into messaging and collateral, and help create programs that support pipeline and revenue generation.

The role covers the full LangChain platform, including Observability & Evaluation, Deployment, Sandboxes, LLM Gateway, Fleet, Engine, and OSS. The goal is to explain how these products work together to help companies build, deploy, monitor, and improve agents in production.

You’ll define the problems we solve for specific audiences, package those into repeatable narratives, and help GTM teams take them to market.

What You’ll Do

Develop industry and use case solutions

  • Build solution narratives for priority industries and enterprise use cases. Initial focus areas include financial services, healthcare, and life sciences, with room to expand based on GTM priorities.

  • Translate customer problems into clear solution stories. You’ll connect LangChain’s platform capabilities to the business, operational, governance, and technical needs of specific audiences.

  • Define repeatable use case messaging. You’ll identify where agents can create value across functions and industries, then turn those patterns into solution briefs, use case pages, campaign assets, sales decks, webinar narratives, and customer-facing content.

  • Build a point of view on enterprise AI adoption. You’ll help explain how companies move from prototypes and isolated experiments to production deployments with the controls, visibility, and evaluation practices they need.

  • Stay close to the market. You’ll synthesize customer conversations, sales feedback, competitive activity, industry trends, and product signals into sharper messaging and GTM recommendations.

Support enterprise GTM motions

  • Partner with sales, solutions, field marketing, demand generation, and customer-facing teams on targeted enterprise campaigns and account motions.

  • Build sales enablement for industry and enterprise conversations. This may include talk tracks, discovery questions, objection handling, use case maps, executive-ready decks, demo narratives, and competitive context.

About the Role

You’ll be LangChain’s first Emerging Talent Recruiter, and you’ll build our intern and new grad program from scratch. Many of the best early-career engineers already build on LangChain and LangGraph. Your job is to hire them first and turn schools, student groups, and campus communities into a lasting pipeline for LangChain.

What You’ll Do

  • Stand up and scale intern and new grad hiring, starting with engineering.

  • Build partnerships with universities, career centers, student groups, and hackathons.

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for interns and new grads, grow into supporting full cycle recruiting for other technical teams

  • Work with leaders to forecast hiring needs and tie each cohort to company priorities.

  • Set up the processes, tools, and metrics we’ll use to track and improve the program.

  • Support with talent brand and marketing initiatives.

What You'll Bring

  • 4+ years of recruiting experience, including 2+ in university or early-career recruiting at a high-growth company.

  • Experience building or scaling an intern or new grad program, with numbers to show for it.

  • Strong relationships with universities and outside partners.

  • Ability to work independently, run several hiring cycles at once, and make decisions with data.

  • Clear communication, including explaining LangChain’s mission to early-career engineers.

Nice to Have

  • Experience recruiting engineering, product, or data talent.

  • Time at an early-stage or venture-backed startup.

  • Experience running campus events, hackathons, or technical programs.

What we offer

  • A blank page. You’re our first hire in this role. You decide how we find, hire, and grow early-career talent.

  • A product students already use. Many of the engineers you’ll recruit already build with LangChain and LangGraph, so you start with real credibility on campus.

  • Room to grow. We’re about 400 people and still growing fast. As the program grows, your scope grows with it.

  • A team that moves. We aim high, ship early, and say what we see. You’ll work with recruiters and hiring managers who move quickly and care about the details.

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

About The Role

The LangSmith team owns and builds LangChain's core platform for observability, evaluation, and production reliability of AI systems. From tracing and annotation to run rules, evaluations, and beyond, this team owns LangSmith end-to-end. If you want to define what great AI observability looks like at production scale, this is where that work gets done.


We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our growing engineering team in Boston. In this role you will be building the backend systems that power LangSmith, LangChain’s observability and evals platform. You will work on the core services that allow our customer's developer teams to monitor and evaluate their AI applications at scale. While the focus is on backend feature development, familiarity with fullstack or frontend engineering, performance tuning, and debugging production issues would be valuable.

This role is based onsite in Boston, MA.

What You'll Do

  • Design, develop, and maintain backend services and APIs to support LangSmith’s tracing, monitoring, and evaluation workflows.

  • Collaborate on architectural decisions to ensure systems are performant and maintainable.

  • Optimize storage and query performance for high-volume observability and evaluation data.

  • Ensure system reliability through strong testing, monitoring, and alerting practices.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve production issues, performing root-cause analysis and implementing long-term fixes.

  • Create and maintain technical documentation, including system design and API references.

  • Work closely with full-stack engineers, product managers, and product designers on rolling out new features.

What You'll Bring

  • 4+ years of professional experience in backend engineering working on highly complex products

  • Proficiency in one or more backend languages/frameworks, ideally Python and/or Go

  • Strong understanding of API design and building reliable data services.

  • Experience with high-throughput, mission-critical systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to optimize backend services for performance and reliability.

  • Experience with database systems (Postgres, Redis, Clickhouse), and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) would be a bonus.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally.

  • Customer centricity and ownership mentality

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

We're looking for a Deployed Engineer to join our Professional Services team, working directly with enterprise customers to build reliable, production agents. You'll translate vague enterprise workflows into concrete software specs and guide engineering teams through the resulting solution, or build it for them. You might spend a week designing a customer's agent architecture, a few weeks co-building their evaluation pipeline, or a quarter embedded inside their team shipping alongside their engineers. You are someone who's built real AI systems for production and can defend the technical tradeoffs within them.

Location: Singapore (Remote with up to 25% travel)

What You'll Do

  • Advising: Agent architecture design, evaluation strategy review, and best-practice production guidance.

  • Building: Co-build with the customer's engineering team across the full Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) in outcome-scoped engagements.

  • Embedding: Serve as a deployed engineer inside the customer's team for extended engagements, operating as a de facto member of their org to ship agent systems directly.

  • Agent Engineering: ADLC end-to-end, architecture design, orchestration patterns, evals, custom conversational UIs, and production deployment.

  • Applied AI: Post-training, supervised fine-tuning, harness engineering, trace mining, model selection and evaluation methodology.

What You'll Bring

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience with deep expertise in Python. TypeScript/JavaScript a plus.

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping production agent systems.

  • Strong client-facing communication skills, with the ability to confidently articulate architectural decisions to technical stakeholders (engineers, architects, CTOs).

  • Strong experience with LangChain/LangGraph/Deep Agents or comparable frameworks, including multi-agent patterns and state management (short and long-term memory).

  • Deep familiarity designing and implementing evaluation methodologies for non-deterministic AI systems.

  • Comfortable operating across the full spectrum from advisory to embedded delivery.

  • Willing to travel up to 20% of the time.

Nice to Have:

  • Exposure to dataset curation and post-training techniques (SFT, DPO, RLHF) on open-weight models using tools like Axolotl, Unsloth, Hugging Face transformers, or TRL.

  • Experience with trace mining to drive continuous improvement loops

Looking to lead technical strategy across the customer journey from Proofs of Value (PoVs) to driving overall adoption? Please check out the Deployed Engineer listing focused on Account Strategy & Solutions.

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

jobs.title: Head of GTM Enablement
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Head of GTM Enablement to build and scale the programs, systems, and habits that help our GTM teams perform. As product delivery accelerates and our portfolio and sales motions grow more complex, you’ll ensure the field keeps pace—turning new capabilities into effective execution without adding unnecessary overhead.

You’ll lead a distributed enablement team and partner with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Product, Customer Engineering, Deployed Engineering, and Revenue Operations. You’ll balance global standards with role and regional needs so priorities translate across regions and roles. Success means faster ramp, stronger field execution, and measurable contributions to pipeline and revenue—not simply more training.

You’ll own the strategy and orchestration behind AI in the field: one consistent, continuously current body of GTM knowledge that the tools other teams build can rely on, so delivery, effectiveness, measurement, and scaling all improve as the field grows. You’ll be equally deliberate about where humans remain essential: the conversations and strategic direction that enabling GTM at large requires.

What You’ll Do

Set the global enablement strategy

  • Define and execute a GTM enablement strategy aligned with revenue growth, customer expansion, and market priorities.

  • Partner with executive and regional leaders to identify capability gaps and execution bottlenecks, directing investment toward the highest-impact opportunities.

  • Own enablement planning, budget, governance, and operating cadence, with clear priorities, ownership, and success measures across onboarding, technical and product enablement, and outbound enablement.

  • Decide where AI changes the enablement model and where human-led work stays, and set the standard the rest of GTM builds against.

Build programs that improve field performance

  • Develop role-based enablement for Account Executives, Account Managers, Sales and Business Development Representatives, Partner/Channel Managers, Customer Engineering, and Deployed Engineering.

  • Tailor programs by segment, industry, and geography where it improves execution, preparing teams to support multiple use cases, buyer types, and platform opportunities.

  • Design and scale role-based 30/60/90-day onboarding that accelerates time to productivity and, for sellers, time to first deal.

  • Establish continuous learning, coaching, and certification programs that reinforce skills beyond onboarding.

  • Embed enterprise sales methodologies into day-to-day workflows, deal reviews, and pipeline inspections.

  • Equip frontline managers to reinforce skills, inspect execution, and coach consistently—making enablement part of how teams operate, not a separate training activity.

  • Structure programs so the knowledge behind them can be reused by AI-assisted practice, reinforcement, and certification, extending reach without proportional headcount.

  • Keep human coaching where it changes behavior, so scalable programs extend reach without replacing the conversations that build skill.

Turn product knowledge into customer value

  • Partner with Product Management and Product Marketing to deliver timely, role-specific training and certification as new capabilities launch.

  • Own the internal training, practice, and reinforcement behind customer-facing messaging and assets, so GTM teams apply them effectively.

  • Turn product and market expertise into practical playbooks, competitive guidance, demo guides, and value-selling resources that are current, easy to find, and useful in customer conversations.

  • Own which assets are canonical, so every team and tool works from the same version as products and markets change.

  • Turn patterns from customer conversations, deal outcomes, and field feedback into updates to that knowledge, so what the field and its tools know keeps improving.

Lead and scale a global team

  • Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team of enablement professionals supporting team members across the Americas, EMEA and APAC.

  • Establish clear decision rights and collaboration practices across global and regional teams, balancing consistency with local market needs and competitive dynamics.

  • Hire and develop for knowledge architecture and program strategy, not just content production, so the function can run without depending on you.

Set the systems vision and own measurement

  • Set the enablement technology vision across learning, content management, and conversation intelligence, and work with GTM Systems and GTM Engineering to execute it, including embedding enablement into workflows.

  • Define what canonical GTM content exists, who maintains it, and how it stays current, so the tools GTM Systems and GTM Engineering build operate from one source instead of diverging copies.

  • Lead the orchestration across GTM Systems, GTM Engineering, Product Marketing, and Revenue Operations, setting requirements for how their tools consume, refresh, and contribute back to that knowledge so quality compounds rather than drifts.

  • Build measurement frameworks and executive reporting that connect enablement investments to skill application, behavior change, pipeline, and revenue outcomes across roles and regions.

  • Use performance data, manager input, and field feedback to continuously improve programs and prioritize resources.

What You’ll Bring

  • 10+ years of relevant experience in GTM enablement within high-growth B2B SaaS organizations, including significant leadership experience.

  • A demonstrated track record of building and scaling global enablement teams and programs across multiple regions.

  • Experience supporting complex enterprise sales motions for technical products, enabling multiple GTM roles across use cases, buyer types, and the full buyer and customer lifecycle.

  • Practical AI fluency, with the judgment to lead strategy and orchestration rather than build tools yourself: what AI can carry, what the knowledge behind it must look like, and where human judgment stays in the loop.

  • Experience standing up or governing a shared knowledge or content system that multiple teams and tools depend on.

  • Deep expertise in enterprise sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, or Value Selling—and a practical approach to embedding them into field execution.

  • Proven success designing onboarding, ongoing learning, product enablement, and manager coaching programs.

  • Experience partnering with systems and engineering teams to deliver enablement technology, with enough fluency to set requirements without owning the platforms yourself.

  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to evaluate program effectiveness and communicate business impact to executive stakeholders.

  • Exceptional communication, storytelling, and cross-functional influence skills.

  • Credibility with field leaders and sellers, and the judgment to know when a conversation or coaching moment will move behavior more than a scalable program.

  • A builder’s mindset: the ability to define strategy, systems, and standards while staying close to execution in a fast-moving environment.

  • Bonus: experience leading or enabling customer-facing technical teams, such as Customer Engineering, Deployed Engineering, or Solutions Engineering, alongside a revenue organization.

How We’ll Measure Success

  • Shorter time to full productivity across GTM roles and faster time to first deal for sellers.

  • Measurable contributions to improved win rates, average contract value, and pipeline velocity.

  • Consistent application of core sales methodologies, reinforced through frontline manager coaching and deal execution.

  • Demonstrated skill development and sustained behavior change—not just participation in training or adoption of tools.

  • Field readiness that keeps pace with product delivery and growing business complexity, with teams prepared to execute on new capabilities, use cases, and sales motions as they launch.

  • AI tools across GTM operating from one current knowledge base, with less rework, drift, and duplicated content, and less administrative work in delivery.

  • Broader enablement coverage at a lower cost per program, showing the field reached more often without proportional headcount.

  • Coaching quality as rated by managers and sellers, not just coaching activity.

  • Improved field and manager satisfaction with enablement, alongside positive trends in GTM team retention.

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

 - Lead the orchestration across GTM Systems, GTM Engineering, Product Marketing, and Revenue Operations, setting requirements for how their tools consume, refresh, and contribute back to that knowledge so quality compounds rather than drifts.

 - Build measurement frameworks and executive reporting that connect enablement investments to skill application, behavior change, pipeline, and revenue outcomes across roles and regions.

 - Use performance data, manager input, and field feedback to continuously improve programs and prioritize resources.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 10+ years of relevant experience in GTM enablement within high-growth B2B SaaS organizations, including significant leadership experience.

 - A demonstrated track record of building and scaling global enablement teams and programs across multiple regions.

 - Experience supporting complex enterprise sales motions for technical products, enabling multiple GTM roles across use cases, buyer types, and the full buyer and customer lifecycle.

 - Practical AI fluency, with the judgment to lead strategy and orchestration rather than build tools yourself: what AI can carry, what the knowledge behind it must look like, and where human judgment stays in the loop.

 - Experience standing up or governing a shared knowledge or content system that multiple teams and tools depend on.

 - Deep expertise in enterprise sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, or Value Selling—and a practical approach to embedding them into field execution.

 - Proven success designing onboarding, ongoing learning, product enablement, and manager coaching programs.

 - Experience partnering with systems and engineering teams to deliver enablement technology, with enough fluency to set requirements without owning the platforms yourself.

 - Strong analytical skills, with the ability to evaluate program effectiveness and communicate business impact to executive stakeholders.

 - Exceptional communication, storytelling, and cross-functional influence skills.

 - Credibility with field leaders and sellers, and the judgment to know when a conversation or coaching moment will move behavior more than a scalable program.

 - A builder’s mindset: the ability to define strategy, systems, and standards while staying close to execution in a fast-moving environment.

 - Bonus: experience leading or enabling customer-facing technical teams, such as Customer Engineering, Deployed Engineering, or Solutions Engineering, alongside a revenue organization.


HOW WE’LL MEASURE SUCCESS

 - Shorter time to full productivity across GTM roles and faster time to first deal for sellers.

 - Measurable contributions to improved win rates, average contract value, and pipeline velocity.

 - Consistent application of core sales methodologies, reinforced through frontline manager coaching and deal execution.

 - Demonstrated skill development and sustained behavior change—not just participation in training or adoption of tools.

 - Field readiness that keeps pace with product delivery and growing business complexity, with teams prepared to execute on new capabilities, use cases, and sales motions as they launch.

 - AI tools across GTM operating from one current knowledge base, with less rework, drift, and duplicated content, and less administrative work in delivery.

 - Broader enablement coverage at a lower cost per program, showing the field reached more often without proportional headcount.

 - Coaching quality as rated by managers and sellers, not just coaching activity.

 - Improved field and manager satisfaction with enablement, alongside positive trends in GTM team retention.

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive (AZ)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Account Executive to join our growing GTM team and drive the next wave of growth at LangChain. In this role, you’ll own the full sales cycle helping technical teams at cutting-edge enterprise companies discover, evaluate, and adopt LangChain’s products.

This is a high-impact, high-visibility role where you’ll collaborate closely with engineering, product, and customer success teams to shape how GenAI is adopted across different domains. If you're a relationship-driven seller who thrives in fast-paced, unstructured environments and wants to be part of building the go-to-market motion from the ground up, we’d love to hear from you.

What You’ll Do

  • Own and manage the full sales cycle, from lead stage to close with a strong bias for follow-up and follow-through

  • Act as a trusted advisor to prospects and customers, learning their needs and demonstrating how our products can solve real problems

  • Drive proof-of-concept efforts, working with sales engineers and product experts to demonstrate tangible value

  • Stay on top of product updates and industry trends to educate customers and shape the conversation around GenAI adoption

  • Build long-term customer relationships and support post-sale success in partnership with our deployment and support teams

  • Negotiate pricing and deal terms and work with legal to redline contracts

  • Bring customer insights back to product and engineering teams to inform the future roadmap and improve the user experience

  • Help define and iterate on our sales playbook - your input will help shape our go to market strategies

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of experience selling complex software to enterprise customers

  • A relationship builder that garners trust quickly and approaches sales with empathy and curiosity

  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills

  • Technical acumen with the ability to establish credibility with technical decision makers.

  • You thrive in fast-paced start-up environments and are energized by impact - you want to help evolve the playbook, not just follow one

  • Driven and solutions-oriented; you know how to navigate roadblocks and keep deals moving forward

  • Passionate about generative AI and excited to help customers navigate a rapidly evolving industry

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

The ways customers buy from us are multiplying as fast as the business is growing. Enterprise order forms. Private offers through AWS, GCP, and Azure. A self-serve business running on usage-based pricing, with commits, drawdowns, and true-ups behind it. Each one is a distinct path from signature to cash, and each one runs today on some mix of manual steps and automation that grew up with the business.

This role owns what comes next, and it's hands-on. You'll run order operations end to end - booking, provisioning, invoicing, amendments, and renewals - and you'll be the business-side admin for Metronome, our metering and billing platform, configuring it to make that work. The rest of the stack is Salesforce for CRM and Rillet for ERP. The stack is modern, but the processes on top of it were built to keep up with growth, not designed to scale. Your job is to decide what each one should become: keep it, rebuild it, automate it, or retire it.

Expect the work to split roughly 80/20. Most of it is operations and process: running the order-to-cash path, fixing what breaks, and getting partner teams onto one roadmap. The other 20% is hands-on systems work: building products and rate cards in Metronome, tracing how deal terms flow from Salesforce into billing, and querying billing data to find what doesn't reconcile. You don't need to be an engineer. You do need to be the kind of operator who opens the admin console and the API docs yourself instead of filing a ticket and waiting.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations and billing configuration, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, Product, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Our bias is to invest in scalable automation rather than a growing queue of manual work, and getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it.

What You'll Do

  • Own order-to-cash end to end: intake, booking, contract setup in Metronome, provisioning, invoicing, amendments, and renewals across Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet

  • Serve as Metronome's primary business admin, shared with Enterprise Engineering: products, rate cards, and custom fields

  • Partner with Deal Strategy and Product to translate new pricing models and non-standard terms into Metronome configuration

  • When a deal won't bill cleanly, decide whether to push back, propose an alternative, or accept a manual process (with a path to automation, or manual by design)

  • Partner with GTM Systems on the data flow from Salesforce to Metronome to Rillet

  • Run cloud marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure, from private offers to disbursement reconciliation

  • Own self-serve billing: plan changes, dunning, credits, rebills, and refunds

  • Be the go-to expert for tracking down and resolving errors in the billing pipeline and Metronome configuration

  • Set the automation roadmap: ship what you can yourself, and get the rest onto partner teams' priorities

  • Build the playbook and audit-ready controls: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exceptions

  • Own three metrics: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years in billing operations, order-to-cash, revenue systems, or billing platform implementation at a B2B SaaS or usage-based company

  • Hands-on admin experience with a usage-based billing platform (Metronome, Stripe Billing, Orb, Chargebee, Zuora, or similar)

  • Working SQL for reconciling billing, usage, and CRM data

  • Comfort with APIs and integrations (no production code required)

  • Deep understanding of usage-based pricing: commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups

  • Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close

  • A track record of learning new systems quickly

  • A history of automating manual work out of your own job

  • Ability to drive cross-team decisions without formal authority

Nice to Have

  • Metronome experience

  • Cloud marketplace experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure private offers)

  • Python or other scripting

  • Building agents or LLM workflows for internal operations, ideally on the LangSmith Platform

  • Audit prep or SOX readiness

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

The stack is modern, but the processes on top of it were built to keep up with growth, not designed to scale. Your job is to decide what each one should become: keep it, rebuild it, automate it, or retire it.

Our bias is to invest in systems rather than in a growing queue of manual work, so you'll be setting the automation roadmap at the same time you're operating the function - deciding what a person should touch, what a workflow should handle, and what should never have been a step in the first place. Getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Those teams are your partners and much of your build capacity. Bringing them onto one shared order-to-cash roadmap is a core part of the job, and the reason we're hiring someone senior to do it.

What You'll Do

  • Own the order-to-cash path end to end: order form intake from Deal Desk, booking in Salesforce, plan and entitlement setup in Metronome, invoicing and revenue recognition through Rillet, and the amendments, true-ups, and renewals that follow

  • Build out cloud marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure: private offer setup, usage reporting to each marketplace, and reconciling marketplace disbursements back to what we billed. Every new channel launches against defined readiness criteria, so marketplace deals run on the same clean path as direct ones

  • Own self-serve billing operations: usage metering, plan changes, dunning, credits, rebills, refunds, and the escalations behind them

  • Own billing and usage completeness at month-end close. Every order, credit, and metered event is reconciled between Metronome and Rillet before revenue is recognized, not after

  • Partner with Deal Strategy and Product as our pricing evolves. Bring the billing view into pricing and deal-structure decisions early, so new models and non-standard terms can be billed accurately and automated, not handled by hand

  • Set the automation roadmap. Instrument the path, put a number on every place a human touches an order, and decide what gets automated, what gets designed away, and what stays manual on purpose

  • Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice

  • Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product

  • Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit

  • Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy

What You'll Bring

  • 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one

  • Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly

  • Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business

  • Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. You don't need to be an accountant, but you should know what Revenue Accounting needs from billing data and why

  • Cloud marketplace experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure private offers), or a track record of getting deep on a system like that fast

  • A history of automating your own job. We'll ask you to walk us through a manual process you deleted: what it cost before, what you built, and what it costs now

  • The ability to build alignment across teams with different priorities and get to a decision, without relying on org authority

  • Comfort shipping a v0 earlier than feels comfortable, then iterating with real feedback

Nice to have

  • SQL, Python, or low-code tooling in your own hands rather than on someone else's backlog

  • Experience building agents or LLM workflows for internal operations. We'd like to run more of our own back office on the LangSmith Platform, wherever it's the right tool and meets the same accuracy bar as the rest of order-to-cash

  • Audit prep or SOX readiness experience

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

 - Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice

 - Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product

 - Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit

 - Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one

 - Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly

 - Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business

 - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. You don't need to be an accountant, but you should know what Revenue Accounting needs from billing data and why

 - Cloud marketplace experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure private offers), or a track record of getting deep on a system like that fast

 - A history of automating your own job. We'll ask you to walk us through a manual process you deleted: what it cost before, what you built, and what it costs now

 - The ability to build alignment across teams with different priorities and get to a decision, without relying on org authority

 - Comfort shipping a v0 earlier than feels comfortable, then iterating with real feedback


NICE TO HAVE

 - SQL, Python, or low-code tooling in your own hands rather than on someone else's backlog

 - Experience building agents or LLM workflows for internal operations. We'd like to run more of our own back office on the LangSmith Platform, wherever it's the right tool and meets the same accuracy bar as the rest of order-to-cash

 - Audit prep or SOX readiness experience

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.




BENEFITS

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

About The Role

The LangSmith team owns and builds LangChain's core platform for observability, evaluation, and production reliability of AI systems. From tracing and annotation to run rules, evaluations, and beyond, this team owns LangSmith end-to-end. If you want to define what great AI observability looks like at production scale, this is where that work gets done.

We’re looking to bring on an experienced frontend engineer to develop and enhance new features on LangSmith, our enterprise platform product for LLM application observability, testing, and debugging.

Location: Onsite in Boston

 

What You'll Do

  • Develop new user-facing features using React & Typescript

  • Build reusable components and front-end libraries for future use

  • Translate designs and wireframes into high-quality code

  • Optimize components for maximum performance across a vast array of web-capable devices and browsers

  • Collaborate with fullstack and backend developers and UX/UI designers, to enhance usability

     

What You'll Bring

  • Extensive front-end engineering experience with strong proficiency in React, JavaScript and TypeScript

  • Hands-on experience with front-end development tools like Babel, Vite, Webpack, NPM, and Yarn

  • Familiarity with REST APIs and experience working closely with fullstack and backend engineers

  • Knowledge of modern authorization mechanisms, such as JWTs

  • A passion for user experience, design and building clean, engaging, and intuitive interfaces

  • Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly and concisely to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • The DNA to thrive in a start-up, fast-paced environment. Views unstructured environments as an opportunity to figure out the most impactful work and help define the future success of the company

  • An ownership mind-set. You are self-driven and look for opportunities to make an impact.

  • Strong computer science fundamentals, ideally with a degree in computer science or related field

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the Role

We're hiring an IT Systems Administrator to join the founding IT team in San Francisco. You'll run most of our SaaS stack day to day, from maintenance and configuration changes to access and troubleshooting. You'll also build the automation that keeps that stack running as we grow.

This is a role for someone who does a bit of everything: helping an employee that’s locked out, shipping a terraform change, and building an automation that removes a manual task. The ideal candidate has startup experience, is comfortable with ambiguity, and heavily leans into automation.

What You'll Do

SaaS Administration

  • Own the day-to-day administration of our SaaS stack, including maintenance, configuration changes, and license management

  • Administer LangSmith, our product, and use APIs to automate admin work

  • Administer identity and permissions across core SaaS platforms such as Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, Zoom, and Microsoft 365

Automation and Tooling

  • Develop scripts, integrations, and reusable workflows using low or no code tools

  • Connect systems through APIs and event-driven workflows to reduce manual work

Identity Management

  • Administer Okta and user access

  • Manage Okta group rules that help define our RBAC policy

  • Establish repeatable standards and automation for employee lifecycle, group management, application provisioning, and access reviews

Client Platform Administration

  • Administer our MDM platform, Iru, to enforce policy configurations, patching, zero-touch deployment, and custom desktop environment configurations

  • Automate the hardware lifecycle from procurement, assignment, return, and recycling

Core IT Operations

  • Provide hands-on troubleshooting and support to employees in the office and remotely across hardware, software, networking, and SaaS tools

  • Build and maintain the harness for our AI ITSM agent, including the tools, playbooks, and knowledge it needs to resolve issues on its own

  • Write documentation and playbooks, and use recurring support issues to guide what to automate next

What You'll Bring

  • 3+ years of experience in IT systems administration or IT engineering, ideally at a fast-growing startup

  • Experience administering a broad SaaS stack that includes Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, and AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT

  • Hands-on experience administering Okta, including SSO, SCIM provisioning, and Okta Workflows

  • Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, and API authentication methods

  • Experience using coding agents (e.g. Claude Code) as part of your day-to-day workflow

  • Experience with a macOS MDM platform and endpoint security tooling

  • Solid networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPNs, wireless)

  • Clear communication, with patience for non-technical users

Compensation Philosophy

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

We’re hiring a Sales Development Manager (New York City or San Francisco) to lead and scale our founding SDR team at LangChain.

Our SDRs play a critical role in helping companies adopt LangChain and LangSmith. They engage technical buyers, convert high inbound interest into qualified opportunities, and work closely with our sales and marketing teams to build pipeline.

This role will own the performance, coaching, and development of the SDR team, while helping design the systems, processes, and workflows that power their GTM motion. You’ll partner closely with sales, marketing, and and RevOps to continuously improve how we identify and engage the right accounts.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and coach a team of SDRs responsible for generating qualified pipeline

  • Own SDR performance including activity metrics, conversion rates, pipeline creation, and attainment

  • Recruit top SDR talent and grow the team as LangChain continues to scale

  • Develop SDR talent through coaching, call reviews, and structured feedback

  • Build repeatable outbound and inbound qualification playbooks

  • Partner with marketing to convert inbound demand into qualified opportunities

  • Work with sales leadership and RevOps to align on target accounts, territories, and pipeline goals

  • Implement systems and workflows that improve SDR productivity and effectiveness

  • Use data to continuously improve performance, analyzing conversion rates across the funnel

What You’ll Bring

  • Have 5+ years of experience in sales development

  • Are comfortable working with technical products and developer audiences

LangChain is hiring a Recruiting Coordinator to help build and scale our high-performing team. You’ll support recruiters, hiring managers, and candidates through every step of the interview and hiring process. You’ll manage interview logistics, drive candidate communication, and keep our recruiting operations running smoothly. You’ll be a key part of creating a thoughtful, efficient, and candidate-friendly hiring experience.

What You'll Do

  • Schedule a high volume of interviews across multiple time zones and mediums (virtual & in-person)
